v1.feedback: The psaltery-string concept is well-integrated into the parent form — vertical string lines pulling particles into vibrating filaments while the rest of the head erodes away reads as a genuine morph rather than a fresh start. The standing-wave harmonics per string and strum envelope show real thought about how the word drives the shader. Two things to tighten: the strum effect builds very slowly (uStrum ramps over ~8s) so for the first several seconds it just looks like the ghostly parent with no psaltery influence — consider starting uStrum higher or adding a subtle initial pluck so the idea lands in the first 2s. The amber/catgut warmth near strings is nice but subtle against the concrete palette; push the string-aligned particles' color contrast a bit more so the strings read as distinct material, not just slightly warmer grey.

v2.feedback: The psaltery-string concept lands well — vertical filaments pulling particles from the ghostly head into vibrating catgut lines is a legible morph that honors both the parent's Salcedo concrete palette and the instrument's form. The standing-wave harmonics per string are a nice touch that earns its compute. Two things to tighten: the erosion/ash-fall of detached particles feels like inherited parent code rather than psaltery-driven design — consider letting eroded particles get caught by neighboring strings instead of just drifting down, reinforcing the instrument metaphor. The amber/catgut color blend could be more restrained; right now the warm tones read a bit uniform across all nine strings — varying warmth or brightness per harmonic would make individual strings more readable and add visual depth.
